transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I have to keep re-checking and re-doing things before and after every drive, or else something terrible will happen and it’ll be my fault. It's just getting really exhausting, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 're-checking and re-doing things' after driving, and what specific terrible things you fear might happen if you don't do these checks?

Before and after every ride, I have to walk around my car checking the doors, trunk, lights, and GPS in a specific order, restarting the whole routine if I get distracted or do it "wrong." I'm terrified that if I don't, I'll miss a red light or a wheel will come off, causing a fatal accident for a family and ruining my entire career.
Do you also experience intrusive thoughts or urges to repeat certain actions or mental acts in other areas of your life, not just related to driving?

The intrusive thoughts actually happen all the time, even when I'm just trying to eat or play a game on my phone, but the thoughts themselves are still always about making driving mistakes. As for the physical checking routines, those are only tied to before and after my driving shifts.

Are the intrusive thoughts and fears you experience limited to driving and the potential consequences of driving mistakes, or do you have other types of obsessive thoughts or fears that are unrelated to driving?

Yes, they are strictly limited to driving and car safety. Even when I'm doing something completely unrelated, like eating or playing a game on my phone, the thoughts looping in my head are still about me missing a red light or not tightening a wheel and causing a fatal crash. I don't really have these obsessive fears about anything else in my life.
Can you describe any compulsions or rituals you feel forced to perform outside of the driving context, even if they're not directly related to driving, to help me better understand your symptoms?

I don't really have any other distinct rituals or compulsions outside of the driving context. All of my checking and re-doing routines are strictly focused on my car, the doors, the trunk, and my GPS before and after my shifts. Outside of that, I don't feel forced to do anything like this.
Have you ever experienced any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning due to these driving-related thoughts and rituals?

Yes, it has completely taken over my life. I've been turning down busy driving shifts and falling way behind on studying for my CDL exam. I've even been bailing on hanging out with my friends because these routines leave me with no time or energy left to do anything else.

You've mentioned that your obsessive thoughts and compulsions are strictly limited to driving and car safety, but can you tell me if you've ever had any periods in your life where you didn't have these driving-related thoughts and rituals, or have they been consistently present over time?

Yeah, I actually didn't have any of these thoughts or rituals before I started driving rideshare heavily. They only started recently after I got into a minor fender-bender in a parking lot and had a really heated argument with a passenger. Before those things happened, I never worried about this stuff at all.
Have you experienced any other types of obsessive thoughts or mental images that are disturbing or violent in nature, outside of the driving-related themes you've mentioned?

No, I haven't experienced any other disturbing thoughts or images like that. My fears are strictly focused on driving, like missing a red light or causing a crash. I don't have those kinds of thoughts about anything else in my life.

Can you tell me if you experience any significant anxiety or distress when you're unable to perform your checking rituals before or after driving, and do you feel like these rituals actually help prevent the terrible things you fear from happening?

If I get distracted or can't finish my routine, my chest gets incredibly tight and I feel this overwhelming sense of dread. Even though I know on some level it might seem excessive, I feel absolutely convinced that doing these checks is the only way to prevent a horrible accident.
Can you describe how long the anxiety and dread last when you're unable to complete your checking rituals, and do you feel like you can ever fully shake off the feeling of impending disaster?

I'm not really sure about the exact timing, but it feels like the anxiety just drags on and on without stopping. It is incredibly hard to shake off that feeling of dread, and it pretty much hangs over me until I'm finally able to go back and do the checks the right way.
Do you believe that your checking rituals are excessive or unreasonable, or do you think they are necessary and make sense given the potential consequences of not performing them?

Logically, a part of me knows that doing these checks over and over is stupid and excessive. But in the moment, the intense fear of causing a catastrophic accident and losing everything makes the routines feel absolutely necessary to prevent a disaster.

Do you think your excessive checking and fear of driving mistakes are part of an illness or a problem that you need help with, or do you see them as a necessary and rational response to the risks of driving?

Deep down, I know these routines aren't rational and I constantly tell myself it's stupid, but I feel completely powerless to stop. It has become a major problem that is taking over my life and ruining my career plans, which is why I finally agreed to seek help after my parents and cousin insisted on it.
Have you ever experienced any intrusive thoughts or images that are unrelated to driving or car safety, even if they are fleeting or seem insignificant to you?

No, I haven't really experienced any intrusive thoughts or images about other things. All of my worries and the pictures that pop into my head are almost entirely focused on driving, car safety, and the fear of causing a terrible accident.

Can you tell me if you have ever experienced any episodes where you felt a sudden, intense urge to shout out or act on an intrusive thought related to driving, or if these thoughts have always been more about fear of consequences rather than urges to act?

No, I've never had any urges to act on those thoughts or shout them out. It is strictly about the fear of making a mistake and the terrible consequences, like causing a horrible accident where someone gets hurt, rather than any desire to do those things on purpose.

Have you ever had any thoughts that you might be a bad person or that you deserve punishment for potentially causing harm to others while driving, even if you know intellectually that these thoughts are not rational?

I don't really think of myself as a "bad person" or focus on being punished, but I do feel an overwhelming dread that a family could die because of my mistake and that it would be entirely my fault. I know intellectually that these looping thoughts are stupid, but I still can't stop them from making my chest feel tight.
